etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle French insidieux, from Latin īnsidiōsus (“cunning, artful, deceitful”), from īnsidiae (“a lying in wait, an ambush, artifice, stratagem”) + -ōsus, from īnsideō (“to sit in or on”), from in (“in, on”) + sedeō (“to sit”).
senses: Causing harm in a stealthy, often gradual, manner.
Intending to entrap; alluring but harmful.
